scope: Documented regional survey campaigns and prospection-window effort profiles separating observed absence from unsurveyed or concealed landscapes.

campaigns.name: Mughal Cholistan archaeological survey
campaigns.method: Systematic pedestrian surface survey along the Hakra paleochannel system
campaigns.coverage_notes: Baseline surface inventory of Cholistan mounds; 25 large reference mounds reused to train Orengo et al. 2020 detector.

campaigns.name: Orengo et al. 2020 Cholistan multi-sensor mound detection
campaigns.investigators: Hector A. Orengo, Francesc C. Conesa, Arnau Garcia-Molsosa, Adam S. Green, Cameron A. Petrie and colleagues
campaigns.method: Random-forest classification of multi-temporal Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery
campaigns.coverage_notes: Proposed 337 mound clusters (71 matched earlier records including 25 reference mounds; 266 unmatched proposals awaiting ground check and chronology).

campaigns.name: Ganweriwala surface surveys and 2024 excavation
campaigns.investigators: Farzand Masih, Toshiki Osada, J. Mark Kenoyer (2007); Sidra Gulzar (2015); University of Lahore / THAAP (2024)
campaigns.method: Total-station surface survey (66.7 ha cultural spread) and 2024 excavation season
campaigns.coverage_notes: Three non-equivalent area figures (81.5 ha legacy, 66.7 ha 2015 cultural spread, circa 33 ha 2020 visible mound) and a 13.7 km DOAM vs survey-paper coordinate discrepancy.

campaigns.name: Green et al. 2019 TwoRains historical-map field survey
campaigns.investigators: Adam S. Green, Hector A. Orengo, Aftab Alam, Arnau Garcia-Molsosa, R. N. Singh, Cameron A. Petrie and colleagues
campaigns.method: Ground verification of Survey of India 19th-20th century topographic mound symbols plus off-map encounters
campaigns.coverage_notes: Checked 779 historical-map features: 199 archaeological positives across multiple periods (169 unlinked to earlier reports) plus 64 off-map locations. Stopping rules in 2017 and map filtering in 2018 restrict transfer of checked rates.

campaigns.name: Land, Water and Settlement and TwoRains projects (Cambridge and BHU)
campaigns.investigators: Cameron A. Petrie, Ravindra N. Singh, Danika Parikh, Jennifer Bates and colleagues
campaigns.region: Rakhigarhi, Masudpur, Lohari Ragho, Bahola, Alamgirpur, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, India
campaigns.method: Multi-season village survey, mound remapping, test excavations, and archaeobotanical flotation
campaigns.coverage_notes: Recorded 127 all-period locations within 15 km of Rakhigarhi and remapped Masudpur from 4 legacy mounds at one coordinate to 13 discrete mounds.

campaigns.name: Garcia-Molsosa et al. 2023 Harappa and Punjab alluvial floodplain survey integration
campaigns.investigators: Arnau Garcia-Molsosa, Hector A. Orengo, Cameron A. Petrie
campaigns.region: Harappa, Khanewal, East Multan and Tulamba, Punjab, Pakistan
campaigns.method: Automated historical-map feature extraction (13,130 raw features; 646 retained) compared against 240 PAS sites and alluvial geomorphology
campaigns.coverage_notes: Matched 123 of 240 PAS all-period sites (51.3%) to historical-map features; distinguished older protohistoric-bearing alluvium from younger scouring channels.

campaigns.name: Harappa Archaeological Research Project (HARP) and earlier ASI excavations
campaigns.investigators: Daya Ram Sahni, M. S. Vats, R. E. M. Wheeler, George F. Dales, Richard H. Meadow, Jonathan Mark Kenoyer
campaigns.method: Long-term stratigraphic urban excavation, surface survey, and conservation
campaigns.coverage_notes: Approximately one quarter of the ancient city lies beneath modern Harappa town (Kenoyer 1991, p. 57).

campaigns.name: Singh et al. 2017 and 2021 Ghaggar-Hakra fluvial coring and OSL dating
campaigns.investigators: Ajit Singh, Kristina J. Thomsen, Rajiv Sinha, Sanjeev Gupta and colleagues
campaigns.region: Kalibangan, Hanumangarh, Sirsa and Haryana foothill paleochannels, India
campaigns.method: Deep sediment coring (36 to 51 m), OSL chronology, and provenance geochemistry
campaigns.coverage_notes: Eight held derived core locations (GS-7, GS-10, GS-11, GS-13, GS-14 near Kalibangan; KNL-1, MNK-6, SRH-5 in Haryana and Punjab). Establishes Sutlej diversion shortly after 8 ka and episodic foothill floods around 3.9 to 3.8 ka.

campaigns.name: Giosan et al. 2012 regional fluvial landscape reconstruction
campaigns.investigators: Liviu Giosan, Peter D. Clift, Mark G. Macklin, Dorian Q. Fuller and colleagues
campaigns.region: Indus Basin from Punjab incised valleys through Sindh to the delta
campaigns.method: SRTM elevation analysis, fluvial geomorphology, and OSL sediment dating
campaigns.coverage_notes: Separates incised Punjab valleys, the stable upper Sindh Indus mega-ridge, and late Holocene burial in southwestern Sindh.

campaigns.name: Mapping Archaeological Heritage in South Asia (MAHSA)
campaigns.investigators: Cameron A. Petrie and MAHSA consortium (Cambridge, Barcelona, partner institutions)
campaigns.region: Indus River Basin and surrounding regions of India and Pakistan
campaigns.method: Arches heritage database compiling legacy site inventories, Survey of India historical map digitization, and field verification
campaigns.coverage_notes: Approximately 10,000 all-period legacy entries reported in 2025. Bulk database not acquired; local API checks held for B02, B04, Hanumangarh, Pilibanga, and Juna Khatiya returned historical map sheet records (Cutch No. 6, Rajputana 44 P 01, Punjab/Rajputana 44 P 05) and no bulk site dump.

campaigns.name: Sindh Directorate of Antiquities and SALU urban rescue at Lakhanjo-daro and Rohri Hills
campaigns.investigators: Shah Abdul Latif University, Directorate of Antiquities Government of Sindh, Paolo Biagi, Elisabetta Starnini
campaigns.region: Sukkur SITE industrial estate and Rohri Hills, Sindh, Pakistan
campaigns.method: Urban salvage trenching (including four 2017 trenches) and flint-quarry landscape survey
campaigns.coverage_notes: Documents industrial truncation of upper deposits alongside surviving lower craft and seal-workshop contexts, plus Rohri Hills quarry landscapes.

campaigns.name: ASI Kutch explorations and Dholavira excavations
campaigns.investigators: J. P. Joshi (1967-1972); R. S. Bisht and ASI (1989-2005)
campaigns.region: Khadir Island, Bela Bet, Surkotada and Kutch mainland, Gujarat, India
campaigns.method: Regional surface reconnaissance and thirteen seasons of urban and cemetery excavation at Dholavira
campaigns.coverage_notes: Anchors Kutch island-belt urbanism and early exploration of Lodrani, Surkotada, and Dholavira.

campaigns.name: University of Kerala, KSKV Kachchh, MSU Baroda, NoGAP and GIAP Kutch surveys and excavations
campaigns.investigators: S. V. Rajesh, G. S. Abhayan, P. Ajithprasad, Francesc C. Conesa, Juan Jose Garcia-Granero and collaborators
campaigns.region: Western Kutch (Juna Khatiya, Padta Bet, Lakhapar), Bela Bet (Kotada in Lodrani), and North Gujarat
campaigns.method: CORONA and historical-map prospection, systematic pedestrian survey, cemetery and habitation excavation
campaigns.coverage_notes: Documented Juna Khatiya cemetery, Padta Bet and Dwajagadh habitation sites, Lakhapar (2026 excavation), and Kotada in Lodrani (alias Morodharo, 2014-2024 explorations).

campaigns.name: Conesa et al. 2014 North Gujarat SAR landscape survey
campaigns.investigators: Francesc C. Conesa, Marco Madella, P. Ajithprasad and colleagues
campaigns.region: Lower Banas, Saraswati and Rupen dune systems, North Gujarat, India
campaigns.method: Multi-temporal SAR seasonal water mapping and NoGAP field integration
campaigns.coverage_notes: Maps seasonal dune and interdune hydrology to target Holocene settlement surfaces.

campaigns.name: Saurashtra and Gulf of Khambhat coastal and estuarine investigations
campaigns.investigators: S. R. Rao; Anjum Farooqui, A. S. Gaur, Vandana Prasad (2013); Archana Das et al. (2022); Ekta Gupta, V. N. Prabhakar (2024); Chintan Vedpathak et al. (2026); NIOT (2003)
campaigns.region: Kaj, Kanjetar, Lothal, Vadgam, Nal corridor, Gulf of Khambhat, Gujarat, India
campaigns.method: Coastal excavation, palynology, AMS-dated estuarine trenching, sea-level index-point synthesis, and offshore sonar/coring
campaigns.coverage_notes: Establishes local marine-to-estuarine retreat downstream of Lothal (4150 +/- 230 BP to 3625 +/- 200 BP) and validates Lothal and Vadgam sea-level index points; offshore Gulf of Khambhat habitation remains unestablished.

campaigns.name: French Archaeological Mission to the Indus Basin (MAFI) and DOAM surveys
campaigns.investigators: Jean-Francois Jarrige, Monique Lechevallier, Aurore Didier, Benjamin Mutin, Pakistan DOAM, Government of Sindh
campaigns.region: Bolan plain (Mehrgarh, Nausharo, Sibri), Chanhu-daro, and Kirthar piedmont (Ghazi Shah, Kai)
campaigns.method: Long-term stratigraphic excavation, piedmont survey, archaeometry, and revised radiocarbon dating
campaigns.coverage_notes: Anchors Bolan alluvial burial (Mehrgarh) and spring-adjacent piedmont sequences (Ghazi Shah); Kai natural cave lacks an authenticated Indus date.

campaigns.name: Makran coastal and Kech-Makran valley surveys
campaigns.investigators: Aurel Stein; George F. Dales (1962); Roland Besenval (1987-1997); Aurore Didier (2014)
campaigns.region: Kech-Turbat valley (Miri Qalat) and Makran coast (Sutkagen-dor, Sotka Koh, Pasni)
campaigns.method: Valley and coastal reconnaissance, stratigraphic excavation at Miri Qalat, tectonic uplift comparison
campaigns.coverage_notes: Approximately 30 Kech-Makran valley sites documented within local traditions; tectonic uplift (1 to 3 m in 1945) and alluvial progradation shift former coastlines inland.

campaigns.name: Biagi coastal shell-midden and Lower Sindh surveys
campaigns.region: Siranda lake, Sonmiani lagoon, Las Bela, Lower Sindh, Pakistan
campaigns.method: Coastal surface survey, shell-midden documentation, and conventional radiocarbon sampling
campaigns.coverage_notes: Records shell middens, lithic scatters, and local stone structures; conventional shell dates lack standardized marine reservoir calibration in our held summary.

campaigns.name: Project 2026-10-12 four-block satellite terrain screening
campaigns.region: Blocks B01 (Ganweriwala), B02 (Harappa), B03 (Juna Khatiya-Padta Bet), B04 (Kalibangan-Pilibanga)
campaigns.method: Copernicus GLO-30 terrain prominence, ESA WorldCover masking, and multi-season Sentinel-2 L2A screening across 740 km2
campaigns.coverage_notes: Reviewed 47 candidates: 42 rejected, 1 known (Kalibangan), 2 context (including B04-T0257 reserve), and 2 unverified screening leads (B01-T0115, B04-T0180). No field verification performed.

prospection_windows.name: Cholistan study-region comparison
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: High documented remote-sensing density (337 Orengo et al. 2020 clusters, 266 unmatched to earlier Cholistan lists), but ground-verified phase attributions and exact cluster coordinates are not held locally. Empty spaces inside P01 outside Mughal's Hakra survey corridor reflect unacquired records and sand-dune cover rather than confirmed absence.

prospection_windows.name: Ganweriwala boundary and surrounding countryside
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Ganweriwala itself has 2007 and 2015 surface surveys plus 2024 excavation, and block B01 screened 200 km2 around the DOAM coordinate (retaining B01-T0115). Absence of recorded sites around Ganweriwala margins reflects dune cover and unacquired Cholistan coordinates rather than sterile ground.

prospection_windows.name: Tohana-Agroha corridor
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Directly covered by Green et al. 2019 historical-map field checks and TwoRains work. Negative checked map features document local non-archaeological features, while off-map encounters (64 across the Green survey) show that unmapped flat or levelled sites remain under-sampled.

prospection_windows.name: Khanauri-Nabha corridor
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Covered by Green et al. 2019 historical-map checks and MAHSA digitization; agricultural levelling and stopping rules after ten negatives per grid cell limit inference of true settlement absence between checked symbols.

prospection_windows.name: Maur-Bathinda-Phul corridor
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Covered by Green et al. 2019 checks; few corpus-inscribed sites fall inside the box because the inscription corpus tracks excavated major sites rather than regional surface scatters.

prospection_windows.name: Sirsa-Hanumangarh valley flanks
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Kalibangan and Karanpura fall inside P06 (with Baror, Binjor, and Tarkhanewala Dera immediately west of 74.0 E), Singh et al. 2017 cored five GS boreholes near Kalibangan, and block B04 screened 196 km2 (retaining B04-T0180 and B04-T0257). Low recorded counts away from the paleochannel reflect alluvial burial, irrigated cultivation, and unacquired MAHSA site entries (local Hanumangarh API query returned map sheets only).

prospection_windows.name: Rakhigarhi-Masudpur rural catchments
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Intensively surveyed by Cambridge and BHU (127 all-period locations within 15 km of Rakhigarhi; Masudpur remapped into 13 mounds). Only a small subset of those 127 surveyed locations enters the inscription-focused gazetteer; low corpus counts reflect non-excavated rural mounds rather than unsurveyed territory.

prospection_windows.name: Harappa-Khanewal, Old Beas and Ganji Bar margins
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Harappa is intensively excavated (HARP) and Garcia-Molsosa et al. 2023 compared 646 map features against 240 PAS sites across the floodplain, plus block B02 screened 144 km2. Apparent gaps on younger alluvial belts reflect channel scouring and burial rather than lack of protohistoric interest.

prospection_windows.name: East Multan-Tulamba interfluves
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Overlaps Garcia-Molsosa et al. 2023 map-extraction frame (P08/P09 shared landforms) and includes Multan's unexcavated early sequence; absence of corpus-inscribed Indus sites reflects lack of acquired PAS coordinates, younger alluvial reworking, and urban burial.

prospection_windows.name: Sukkur-Rohri urban and industrial fringes
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Contains excavated Kot Diji and salvage-trenched Lakhanjo-daro in the Sukkur SITE industrial zone (with Naru-Waro-dharo immediately west of 68.7 E) plus Biagi's Rohri Hills quarry surveys. Absence of surface finds inside Sukkur reflects industrial construction cover and truncation, not absence of ancient occupation.

prospection_windows.name: Lower Indus ridge and backswamp margins
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Contains major excavated sites along the margins (Amri, Chanhu-daro, Lohumjo-daro), while lower Sindh backswamps and migrating channels have only regional geomorphic synthesis (Giosan et al. 2012) and no systematic coring archive in our held records. Empty interior cells are unsurveyed or buried beneath late Holocene alluvium.

prospection_windows.name: Western Kutch, Juna Khatiya-Padta Bet-Lakhapar catchments
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Active fieldwork by University of Kerala, KSKV Kachchh, and GIAP at Juna Khatiya, Padta Bet, Dwajagadh, and Lakhapar inside P12 (with Desalpar and Khirsara just south of 23.5 N), plus block B03 screening (200 km2) and held MAHSA historical map sheet Cutch No. 6. Gaps outside surveyed catchments remain untested for small habitation sites paired with cemeteries.

prospection_windows.name: Bela Bet and Lodrani tributary margins
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Anchored inside P13 by 2014-2024 explorations at Kotada in Lodrani (Morodharo) on Bela Bet, with ASI excavations at Dholavira, Pabumath, and Surkotada in adjacent Kutch blocks. Tributary margins outside known fortified mounds lack systematic published survey coverage in our held holdings.

prospection_windows.name: Lower Banas-Saraswati-Rupen dune systems
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Covered by Conesa et al. 2014 SAR hydrology mapping and Nagwada excavation near the southern edge, but full NoGAP surface-survey site tables are not held locally. Empty interior cells reflect unacquired survey records and aeolian dune concealment.

prospection_windows.name: Kaj-Kanjetar mid-Saurashtra estuaries
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Anchored by Prabhas Patan and coastal excavations at Kaj and Kanjetar (Farooqui et al. 2013, coordinates unheld). Absence of recorded sites across intervening mid-Saurashtra estuaries reflects lack of systematic coastal-corridor survey data and Holocene shoreline shift.

prospection_windows.name: Kech-Turbat tributary fans
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Anchored by French excavations at Miri Qalat and Besenval's regional reconnaissance (~30 multi-period valley sites, individual coordinates not held). Empty cells reflect unacquired survey lists and flash-flood alluvial burial in tributary fans.

prospection_windows.name: Bolan outlet-Dhadar-Nausharo fan margins
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Anchored by French Mission excavations at Mehrgarh, Nausharo, Sibri, and Pirak. Fan margins away from the Bolan river-cut sections remain concealed beneath thick piedmont alluvium where surface survey has low detection probability.

prospection_windows.name: Kirthar piedmont, Jamshoro-western Dadu
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Covered by MAFI Kirthar piedmont work, DOAM Ghazi Shah inventory, and Sindh 2015 cultural property inventory (including Kai cave). Piedmont fans and interfluves remain unevenly surveyed; absence of dated Indus cave occupation reflects lack of stratified dating rather than exhaustive testing.

prospection_windows.name: Siranda-Sonmiani lagoon margins
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Anchored by Balakot and Bakkar Buthi plus Biagi's shell-midden reconnaissance around Siranda and Sonmiani (individual midden coordinates not held). Gaps reflect delta advance, dune cover, and unacquired survey tables.

prospection_windows.name: Khambhat gulf, Lothal-Vadgam estuary landscapes
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Anchored by Lothal, Rangpur, Kanewal, and recent estuarine coring and sea-level synthesis (Das et al. 2022; Gupta et al. 2024; Vedpathak et al. 2026). Low counts along buried paleochannels and offshore areas reflect estuarine siltation and submergence rather than confirmed absence.

prospection_windows.name: Makran Dasht-Sutkagen Dor to Pasni coast
prospection_windows.absence_interpretation: Anchored by Sutkagen-dor and Sotka Koh from Dales 1962 coastal reconnaissance and tectonic uplift observations at Pasni. Intervening Makran coastal terraces and inland paleoshorelines have no systematic modern survey inventory in our held records.
